## Design

### 2026-10-24 – Date: October 23, 2026

**2h**

Date: October 23, 2026

In this session, I started by considering which main controller board to use and ended up going with the Xiao ESP32-S3 because it's cheaper, but it also limits how many parts I can connect to it. Knowing that the number of parts is limited, I decided to go for at least one of each part to get experience with new parts when assembling them together. One thing that confused me for a bit was the wiring and labels because I had to get the right labels and make sure I had enough ports on the Xiao to make everything connect. After everything was connected, I had a Xiao microcontroller board, two switches, two LEDs, five touch pads, one potentiometer, and one rotary encoder switch. This concludes the parts layout session, and in the next session, I will be assigning the footprints and starting to design the actual PCB.
